summary: Los Padres lookout in Monterey County: CCC-built in 1934, staffed until 1958, torn down after the land went to the Army; remnants reported on the south summit.

facts.design: Ten-foot enclosed timber tower with a 14x14 cab, California Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin
facts.status_note: Discontinued in 1958; land traded to the Army and the structure torn down later. A hiker's undated trip report found remnants on the south summit.

access.note: Register says the land was traded to the US Army but still lists the Forest Service as administrator; no current access rule found in the sources

visit.drive_up: Dirt South Coast Ridge Road passes the site; the trip report says high clearance would have helped
visit.trail_note: The old road to the south summit is badly overgrown but has a serviceable use trail

events.note: Constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps for the US Forest Service

corrections.proposed: 1958 staffed_last; removal after 1958 with no exact year given
corrections.why: The register says 'After 1958' for removal. 1958 is the year the lookout was discontinued, not a removal date.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the land was traded to the Army and lists the Forest Service as administrator. No source we read confirms the current arrangement. A hiker's undated trip report says the writer was told on the summit that they were on federal property, but that happened at the Alder Peak antenna site, not at Three Peaks, so it does not bear on this lookout.

notes_for_editor: Staffing and removal are well sourced from the register and the Forest Lookouts page (which quotes a 1988 book). Today's condition rests on one undated trip report, so the remnants may have changed. The 'federal property' remark in that report was made at Alder Peak, so it was removed from this story and access moved from 'restricted' back to 'unknown': the land went to the Army, but no current rule was found. The trip report places the lookout on the south summit, not the highpoint, which matches the remnants it describes.
